title: A diagnosis at three, ending the poor-nutrition myth
first: A three-year-old boy in a remote village in Madhya Pradesh was losing strength in his legs. Far from any specialist hospital, his family and local providers took it for severe malnutrition. An NGO collected a dried blood spot and arranged a molecular test with us: Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
impact: Ended the search for a diagnosis, and treatments that could not help.
Connected him to medical care and physiotherapy to preserve mobility.
Carrier testing and genetic counselling for his mother and family.

title: Two carriers, one plan
first: A young couple in Chhattisgarh had lost their first child in infancy to progressive muscle weakness, never diagnosed. In their second pregnancy a government screening programme referred them to us. Carrier testing showed both parents carry the SMN1 deletion behind spinal muscular atrophy.
impact: Timely prenatal genetic diagnosis in the second pregnancy.
Genetic counselling and a clear plan for the couple and their obstetrician before birth.

title: Replacing fate with informed prevention
first: In a village in Odisha, a young couple had watched two children in their extended family suffer severe anaemia, painful crises and repeated infections, put down locally to fate. Community dried blood spot screening showed both partners carry sickle cell trait (AS).
impact: Counselling explained their 25% risk of a child with sickle cell disease (SS) in each pregnancy.
Linked to prenatal diagnosis, with clinical follow-up and nutritional care for the affected children.
